[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/Platform-Web%20%7C%20Mini--games%20%7C%20Playable%20ads%20%7C%20Desktop%20%7C%20Android%20%7C%20iOS-green.svg)](https://estellaengine.com/docs/publishing/overview/)
[![Ask DeepWiki](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ask-DeepWiki-1f6feb.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/esengine/estella)

<img src="docs/assets/icons/globe.svg" width="18" height="18" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> [Website](https://estellaengine.com)  ·  <img src="docs/assets/icons/bot.svg" width="18" height="18" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> [Agent](#your-agent-drives-the-editor)  ·  <img src="docs/assets/icons/rocket.svg" width="18" height="18" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> [Getting Started](#getting-started)  ·  <img src="docs/assets/icons/book-open.svg" width="18" height="18" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> [Documentation](#documentation)  ·  <img src="docs/assets/icons/message-circle.svg" width="18" height="18" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> [QQ群 481923584](https://qm.qq.com/q/BONa5LXQ0U)

<br/>

<img src="docs/assets/agent-e58817d7.webp" alt="An AI agent driving the Estella editor over MCP: it opens the Bistro project, finds the Weather entity and turns it to snow, sets the time of day to 9 pm, presses Play, steps the game and takes a screenshot of the snowy night it made" width="900" />

<sub><i>Every frame is one MCP tool call into the editor, captured as it happened — no mouse involved.</i></sub>

</div>

<a id="your-agent-drives-the-editor"></a>

## <img src="docs/assets/icons/bot.svg" width="26" height="26" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Your agent drives the editor

The Estella editor speaks the **Model Context Protocol**. Connect Claude Code, Cursor,
Codex or any MCP client, and the agent works inside the real editor rather than
around it:

- <img src="docs/assets/icons/hammer.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **It builds** — creates projects, spawns entities from the editor's own Create catalog,
  writes component fields, makes prefabs, paints tilemaps, writes and type-checks scripts.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/eye.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **It looks** — takes screenshots of the viewport and the running game, replays a frame
  draw by draw, compares the game with reference images, and audits what a scene's look lacks.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/play.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **It plays** — enters Play mode, steps time deterministically, sends input and clicks
  UI by name, runs scripted playtests, then reads the running world back.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/palette.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **It makes assets** — images, sound effects, music and 3D models, each answered with
  a picture of what it made.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/rocket.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **It ships** — reads project health, exports the game, and drives a build running on a
  connected phone.

Every call goes through the editor's command surface: each one is **one undo step**,
you watch it happen in the window, and you can take the mouse back at any time. The
editor starts **read-only**; an agent edits only after you allow it in
*Window → Connect AI Tools…*, which also writes the client's MCP config for you.

| Group | What the agent gets |
|---|---|
| core | scene tree, entities, components, play / step / input, screenshots, logs, undo |
| `assets` · `prefab` · `authoring` | asset documents and import settings, tilemaps, prefabs and variants, physics bodies, UI events |
| `look` · `render` | reference images beside the game, light and field sweeps, frame capture and replay, shadows, LOD, bakes |
| `code` · `project` | scripts, symbol search, type-check, project settings, health, export |
| `image` · `sound` · `modeling` | draw sprites and textures, compose sound and music, build 3D models from steps |
| `play` · `view` · `device` | gamepads, time scale, scripted playtests, editor view, and a game running on a connected phone |

→ [Connecting an agent](https://estellaengine.com/docs/agents/mcp/)

## <img src="docs/assets/icons/shield-check.svg" width="26" height="26" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Why Estella, when Unity and Unreal have MCP too?

An MCP server can be bolted onto any editor. What an agent can actually get done
depends on what sits behind it.

- <img src="docs/assets/icons/plug.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **The protocol is the editor, not a plugin on it.** The 167 tools call the pipelines the
  editor's own menus, inspector and toolbar run, so an agent's edit is the edit a person
  would have made, and undoes the same way. Calls are schema-checked and permission-gated
  by the editor itself.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/eye.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **The agent can check its own work.** It steps a paused game frame by frame, so
  "play three seconds, then look" is the same frame every run. It sees the game, not just the
  log: screenshots, a frame replayed draw call by draw call, the game set beside a reference
  image, scripted playtests that read the running world back.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/wand-sparkles.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **The agent can make what the game needs.** Sprites, textures, sound effects, music and
  3D models come from tools inside the editor, so a prototype does not stop at grey boxes
  while someone opens five other programs.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/file-text.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Everything is text.** Scenes, prefabs and materials are JSON; gameplay is TypeScript.
  An agent reads and writes the project directly, and every change is a reviewable diff.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/globe.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **It ships where heavier engines struggle.** A WebAssembly runtime that loads on a phone
  browser, seven Chinese mini-game platforms, single-file playable ads for the major ad
  networks, and native Android / iOS apps — from one project.
- <img src="docs/assets/icons/scale.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **It is open.** The runtime, SDK, pipeline and CLI are Apache-2.0: no royalties, no seats,
  no runtime fees. The editor is a free download.

## <img src="docs/assets/icons/camera.svg" width="26" height="26" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Rendered in real time

<div align="center">
  <img src="docs/assets/day-1ea1637f.webp" alt="The Bistro street corner rendered in real time by Estella from morning to night: a low sun, mist, rain that leaves puddles with rings on the water and splashes on the street, then snow settling on the awnings and falling past the lit street lamps" width="900" />
  <br/>
  <sub><i>One day on the Amazon Lumberyard Bistro, recorded frame by frame from the running game: a sun that follows the clock, weather that turns from clear to mist, rain and snow, baked bounce light, reflections and volumetric haze. Scene © Amazon Lumberyard, <a href="https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/">CC BY 4.0</a>, modified.</i></sub>
</div>

<div align="center">
  <a href="https://github.com/esengine/estella-space-frigate"><img src="docs/assets/space-frigate-efc7716b.webp" alt="Space Frigate, a game made with Estella: a frigate cruises off a gas giant, turns on her thrusters, fires her turrets at an asteroid, then flies through a gate, down a tunnel of light, and comes out beside a ringed ice giant" width="900" /></a>
  <br/>
  <sub><i><a href="https://github.com/esengine/estella-space-frigate">Space Frigate</a>, a game made with Estella and recorded frame by frame as it runs: flying on thrusters, gunnery, and a jump through a gate to another star system. Every model, texture and sound in it is generated from a recipe.</i></sub>
</div>

## <img src="docs/assets/icons/layers.svg" width="26" height="26" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> What's inside

Estella is a C++ engine with a TypeScript SDK. The core runs as WebAssembly on the web
and natively on desktop and mobile; game logic is written as ECS systems in TypeScript.

<img src="docs/assets/icons/layers.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **2D** — sprites and sprite animation, tilemaps (with LDtk import), Spine 2.1 – 4.3 and
DragonBones, 2D lights and shadows, UI with layout, rich and bitmap text, particles,
Box2D physics, native 2D rigs.

<img src="docs/assets/icons/box.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **3D** — glTF / FBX import, PBR materials, directional / point / spot lights with
shadows, sky atmosphere with time of day and weather, baked lightmaps, light and
reflection probes, SSR, SSGI, height fog, terrain, water, foliage, skeletal animation
with spring bones, navigation, Jolt or PhysX physics, streamed large worlds.

<img src="docs/assets/icons/globe.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Everywhere** — one renderer for 2D and 3D on WebGL 2 and WebGPU, and one project
exports to:

| Target | What you get |
|---|---|
| <img src="docs/assets/icons/globe.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Web | a static, self-contained build |
| <img src="docs/assets/icons/gamepad-2.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Mini-games | WeChat, Douyin, Kuaishou, Bilibili, Alipay, Huawei and quick games |
| <img src="docs/assets/icons/megaphone.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Playable ads | one inlined `index.html` for Meta, Google, Unity, AppLovin, Mintegral, TikTok / Pangle and MRAID networks |
| <img src="docs/assets/icons/monitor.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Desktop | a native app on Windows, macOS and Linux — no Chromium |
| <img src="docs/assets/icons/smartphone.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Android / iOS | a native arm64 app on Vulkan / Metal — not a WebView |

<a id="getting-started"></a>

## <img src="docs/assets/icons/rocket.svg" width="26" height="26" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Getting Started

<img src="docs/assets/icons/download.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Install.** Download the editor for Windows or macOS from
[estellaengine.com](https://estellaengine.com/#download) — always the newest release.
Every build is also on the [releases page](https://github.com/esengine/estella/releases).

<img src="docs/assets/icons/folder-plus.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Create a project.** Open the editor, click **New Project**, pick a template.

<img src="docs/assets/icons/code.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> **Write a system.**

```typescript
import {
    defineComponent, defineSystem, addSystem,
    Query, Mut, Res, Time, LocalTransform
} from 'esengine';

const Speed = defineComponent('Speed', { value: 200 });

addSystem(defineSystem(
    [Res(Time), Query(Mut(LocalTransform), Speed)],
    (time, query) => {
        for (const [entity, transform, speed] of query) {
            transform.position.x += speed.value * time.delta;
        }
    }
));
```

<img src="docs/assets/icons/play.svg" width="20" height="20" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Press **F5** to play — or connect your agent and ask it to do all three.

## <img src="docs/assets/icons/book-open.svg" width="26" height="26" align="absmiddle" alt="" /> Documentation

## Ways to Use It

| Surface | Get it | Docs |

![World Monitor terminal dashboard](docs/images/tui/overview.webp)

---

## What It Does

- **Curated news feeds** across global and regional categories, AI-synthesized into briefs
- **Dual map engine** — 3D globe (globe.gl) and WebGL flat map (deck.gl) with a shared map-layer catalog
- **Panel inventory** — concrete panel implementations across specialized variants
- **Cross-stream correlation** — military, economic, disaster, and escalation signal convergence
- **[Country Instability Index (CII)](https://www.worldmonitor.app/country-instability-index/)** — live CII v14 scores, bands, and approximate 24-hour movement for 31 Tier-1 countries
- **Finance radar** — stock exchanges, commodities, crypto, and a market composite
- **Local AI** — run everything with Ollama, no API keys required
- **Site variants** from a single codebase (world, tech, finance, commodity, happy, energy)
- **Native desktop app** (Tauri 2) for macOS, Windows, and Linux
- **Multilingual UI** with native-language feeds and RTL support

For the full feature list, architecture, data sources, and algorithms, see the **[documentation](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/documentation)**.

---

## Support Status

All site variants and desktop binaries are built from a single codebase and ship from the same release process. The table below clarifies maintenance status so you know which surfaces are safe to depend on.

| Surface | Status | Notes |
|---------|--------|-------|
| `worldmonitor.app`, `tech.`, `finance.`, `commodity.`, `happy.`, `energy.` | Stable | Public deployments built from this repo, actively maintained |
| Desktop binaries (Windows / macOS Apple Silicon / macOS Intel / Linux AppImage x64 and ARM64) | Stable | One Tauri binary for every variant — install World Monitor and switch to tech, finance, commodity, energy, or happy in-app. There is deliberately no per-variant download |
| `worldmonitor` npm package (terminal dashboard and CLI) | Stable | Published from [`cli/`](cli/) on every `cli-v*` tag |

Issues filed against any of the above are triaged from the same backlog — see the [issues board](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/issues) for currently-open work.

---

## Quick Start

**One-line install** (self-host the full stack with Docker — dashboard, Redis, AIS relay, seeded public data):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://www.worldmonitor.app/install.sh | bash
```

This clones into `./worldmonitor` (or reuses your checkout), generates the required secrets, starts the stack, and seeds data. Then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Options: `--dir`, `--port`, `--no-seed`, `--no-build`, passed after `bash -s --` (see `scripts/install.sh --help`). API keys are optional. Details, production notes, and uninstall: [SELF_HOSTING.md](./SELF_HOSTING.md).

**Local development** (hot-reload Vite server):

Requires Node.js 24, the version pinned in `.nvmrc`. Distribution packages are often older. Debian 12 and Raspberry Pi OS ship Node.js 18 with npm 9.2.0, where `npm install` stops with `Invalid comparator: file:vendor/braces`. Install Node.js 24 with [nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm) (`nvm install` inside the checkout reads `.nvmrc`) or from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor.git
cd worldmonitor
npm install
npm run dev
```

Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) (override the port with `DEV_PORT` in `.env.local`). The app runs with no environment variables.

Feature-specific data sources may require credentials. See `.env.example` for the full list.

For variant-specific development:

```bash
npm run dev:tech       # tech.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:finance    # finance.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:commodity  # commodity.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:happy      # happy.worldmonitor.app
npm run dev:energy     # energy.worldmonitor.app
```

See the **[self-hosting guide](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/getting-started)** for deployment options (Vercel, Docker, static).

|----------|-------------|
| **Frontend** | Vanilla TypeScript, Vite, globe.gl + Three.js, deck.gl + MapLibre GL |

| **AI/ML** | Ollama / OpenRouter, Transformers.js (browser-side) |
| **API Contracts** | Protocol Buffers and sebuf HTTP annotations |
| **Deployment** | Vercel Edge Functions, Railway relay, Tauri, PWA |
| **Caching** | Redis (Upstash), 3-tier cache, CDN, service worker |

Full stack details in the **[architecture docs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/architecture)**.

---

## Programmatic Access

World Monitor is built for agents and scripts as well as browsers:

- **MCP server** — `https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Public `tools/list`; `tools/call` authenticates with a `X-WorldMonitor-Key` header or OAuth.
  The server also publishes its Agent Skills through the draft `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` extension (`skills/list`, `skills/get`, and `skill://…` resource reads).

Gemini custom apps and Connected Apps sign in through Google's OAuth callbacks. See [Gemini and Antigravity](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/gemini-antigravity).
- **REST API** — base `https://api.worldmonitor.app`, described by the [OpenAPI spec](https://worldmonitor.app/openapi.yaml).
- **CLI** — the official [`worldmonitor`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/worldmonitor) npm package (source in [`cli/`](cli/)). Run it with no arguments in a terminal for the [terminal dashboard](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli-dashboard):

  ```sh
  npx worldmonitor tools          # run ad-hoc — list every MCP tool (no key needed)
  npm install -g worldmonitor     # or install the `worldmonitor` (alias `wm`) command
  brew install worldmonitor       # or install it with Homebrew
  worldmonitor risk IR --api-key wm_xxx
  ```

- **SDKs** — official zero-dependency client libraries mirroring the CLI: Python [`worldmonitor-sdk`](https://pypi.org/project/worldmonitor-sdk/) (source in [`sdk/python/`](sdk/python/)), Ruby [`worldmonitor`](https://rubygems.org/gems/worldmonitor) ([`sdk/ruby/`](sdk/ruby/)), Go [`github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go) ([`sdk/go/`](sdk/go/)). ## Features

### Apps

- **Email**: Custom domain mailboxes, personal or shared, with access you control. Send and receive with Cloudflare Email, Resend or Amazon SES.
- **Routing rules**: Store, forward, reject or sort incoming mail.
- **Calendar**: Repeating events with time zones. Attendees get email invitations.
- **Booking**: Share a public link so anyone can book a free time on your calendar.
- **Drive**: Store and share files.
- **AI agents**: Search mail, draft replies and manage events. Connect other AI tools over MCP.

### Technical

- **Databases**: Cloudflare D1 (default), PostgreSQL, MySQL, Turso / libSQL, or a local SQLite file. Set `DATABASE_URL` to switch. Works with Supabase, Neon, PlanetScale, TiDB and more. See [Databases](docs/databases.md).
- **File storage**: Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2 or AWS S3.
- **Hosting**: Cloudflare Workers or a single Docker container.
- **Admin**: Users, API keys, webhooks, audit logs and backups.
- **Import**: Bring in mail from IMAP, Gmail Takeout, `.eml` and `.mbox` files.

Mailflare currently supports 34 languages, including English, Português (Brasil), Português (Portugal), Español, Français, Deutsch, Italiano, Nederlands, Polski, Українська, Русский, Türkçe, 中文（简体）, 日本語, 한국어, Bahasa Indonesia, Bahasa Melayu, Tiếng Việt, ไทย, हिन्दी, বাংলা, मराठी, తెలుగు, தமிழ், ગુજરાતી, ಕನ್ನಡ, മലയാളം, ਪੰਜਾਬੀ, සිංහල, Kiswahili, Hausa, plus العربية, اردو and فارسی (right-to-left).

You can receive and send mail for free.

- **Receiving**: Cloudflare Email Routing is free.
- **Sending**: Use the free tier of Resend (3,000 emails a month) or Amazon SES. Cloudflare's own sending needs the $5/month Paid Worker plan.

New Amazon SES accounts start in a sandbox. Ask AWS for production access to lift it. Prices change, so check [Resend](https://resend.com/pricing), [Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/pricing/) and [Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/pricing/).

## Deploy

1. **Deploy the app.** Click **Deploy to Cloudflare**. Keep the app name `mailflare`, or it will break.
2. **Finish setup.** Open the app at `/setup` and create your admin account.
3. **Connect a domain.** Add a domain from the same Cloudflare account, then create your first mailbox.

> **`CF_TOKEN` is required.** Create a scoped [Cloudflare API token](https://github.com/hieunc229/mailflare/issues/24#issuecomment-5523686105) with these permissions:
>
> - All accounts: Email Sending:Edit, DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Addresses:Edit
> - All zones: DNS Settings:Edit, Email Routing Rules:Edit, Zone Settings:Edit, DNS:Edit

```text
2. Ask me for my Cloudflare account ID and two API tokens, using a secret input:
   a deploy token (for Wrangler) and a runtime token (the Worker secret CF_TOKEN).
   Never print them, commit them, or pass them as command arguments.
3. Keep the Worker name exactly "mailflare". Create or reuse the D1 database
   "mailflare", the R2 bucket "mailflare-raw", and the queues "mailflare-inbound",
   "mailflare-outbound" and "mailflare-agent".
4. Install dependencies, run `npm run deploy`, and set CF_TOKEN as a Worker secret.
   Do not run remote database migrations yourself. The /setup page does that.
5. Give me the app URL and anything I still need to do. I will open /setup, create
   the admin account and connect my domain.
```

Token permissions and more options: [deployment guide](docs/deployment.md#deploy-with-an-ai-coding-agent).

### Self-host with Docker

Runs as one container on any server, with SQLite and local files.

Add your Cloudflare credentials to `.dev.vars`, then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Run `npm run db:seed` to load sample data.

## Development Setup

### Prerequisites

- Install [Node.js] which includes [Node Package Manager][npm]

### Setting Up a Project

Install the Angular CLI globally:

```
npm install -g @angular/cli
```

Create a workspace:

```
ng new [PROJECT NAME]
```

Run the application:

```
cd [PROJECT NAME]
ng serve
```
